limitations: The exact transaction is canonical, but the original negotiation chat has not been recovered.
Robert's current recollection is unusually specific about the objective and quarterback decision, but it is still a 2026 reconstruction rather than contemporaneous documentation.
The later player outcomes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, CeeDee Lamb, Jahmyr Gibbs, Marvin Harrison Jr., Jordan Love and Rome Odunze are excluded from the ex-ante reconstruction.
Robert remembers the executed price as cheap, but not a separately pre-defined hard maximum price or walk-away ceiling.

evidence_basis.note: Confirms the completed startup position swap and exact original pick assets.

Robert remembers the trade objective very clearly: secure a long-term dynasty quarterback anchor so he would not need to keep solving QB. His intended elite-QB set was Patrick Mahomes or Josh Allen. He was highly confident in the trade-up concept, while the later Mahomes-versus-Allen selection itself felt materially less certain.

Robert recalls preferring Mahomes after acquiring 1.01 because Mahomes felt like the safer established dynasty bank; Allen offered clear rushing upside but Robert had concerns about the durability/sustainability of the rushing style and whether Allen would fully establish himself at that level. This is a draft-selection rationale nested inside, but distinct from, the trade-up decision.

Robert clarifies that 1.01 mattered because he explicitly wanted control of the quarterback selection rather than simply accepting whichever of Mahomes or Josh Allen remained at 1.02. He considered the executed price cheap, with only small later-round position concessions. He rates the trade decision itself 5/5 confidence and the ex-ante outcome uncertainty 2/5.

decision_context.objective: Move from startup 1.02 to 1.01 so Robert could control the elite quarterback selection himself and lock in a long-term dynasty QB anchor.
decision_context.roster_context: This was the startup draft in the league's original one-quarterback setting. Robert wanted to establish the most important long-term quarterback slot immediately rather than revisit the position repeatedly.
decision_context.cap_salary_context: No salary/cap system was part of Robert's recalled rationale for this startup trade.
decision_context.team_window: The league was at dynasty inception, so the objective was foundational multi-year roster construction rather than a short contender/rebuild window.
decision_context.market_context: Robert's elite target set was Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen, but the value of 1.01 was specifically the ability to choose between them rather than accept whichever player remained at 1.02. After acquiring 1.01, the Mahomes-versus-Allen player decision itself remained materially less certain than the trade-up.
decision_context.why_now: The startup 1.01 gave Robert full control over the elite quarterback choice at dynasty inception, which he valued more than passively taking the remaining option at 1.02.
constraints: The trade exchanged Robert's original 1.02/2.05/6.05 positions for Tim's 1.01/2.06/6.06 positions, so control of 1.01 cost only one slot in Round 2 and one slot in Round 6.
Robert explicitly considered those later position concessions small and the overall price cheap.

theses.statement: In a dynasty startup, paying small later-round position concessions to control 1.01 was clearly worthwhile because Robert wanted to choose his long-term elite quarterback himself.
falsification_conditions: Control of the Mahomes-versus-Allen choice had little meaningful value relative to simply remaining at 1.02.
The later-round position concessions materially outweighed the value of controlling 1.01.

theses.statement: The strategic value of the trade came from agency over the elite-QB selection, not merely from being guaranteed one of Mahomes or Josh Allen.
falsification_conditions: Robert would have been equally satisfied to let Tim choose first and simply take the remaining quarterback.
Robert did not actually value the ability to select the preferred quarterback at 1.01.

alternatives.description: Remain at startup 1.02 and take whichever elite quarterback remained after Tim's 1.01 selection.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert explicitly wanted to make the Mahomes-versus-Allen decision himself rather than surrender control of the choice.

price_ceiling.description: Robert remembers the executed swap as cheap: move from 1.02 to 1.01 in exchange for moving one slot later in Round 2 and one slot later in Round 6. He does not remember a separately defined hard maximum price.

known_risks.description: Because both Mahomes and Josh Allen were acceptable elite targets, the marginal value of controlling the exact choice at 1.01 could have been smaller than Robert perceived.
The long-term value thesis depended on an elite quarterback actually providing the positional stability Robert expected in the league's then one-QB format.

decision_state_at_execution.confidence_rationale: Robert remembers the trade-up itself as a clear decision: he wanted control of the elite-QB choice, considered the price cheap and would have executed the same move without hesitation. The uncertainty was concentrated in the later Mahomes-versus-Allen player selection, not in acquiring 1.01.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_confidence_driver: Full control over selecting the preferred long-term elite quarterback at a very low perceived move-up cost.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_source_of_doubt: The trade itself carried little remembered doubt; the meaningful uncertainty began only after the trade when choosing Mahomes versus Josh Allen.
known_personal_biases: Strong preference for long-term positional security and for retaining agency over the elite quarterback choice.
